requirement: Under {cite}`requirements.cli.skill_structure`, the `habeas` skill MUST be the home of routing tasks to skills, `habeas status` and `habeas info`, directive and reference syntax, distributed requirements, and gotchas common to every task.
rationale:
**Obligation.** `requirements.cli.skill_structure.habeas` says the `habeas` skill MUST be the home of five topics: task routing, `habeas status` and `habeas info`, directive and reference syntax, distributed requirements, and gotchas common to every task. The cited parent, `requirements.cli.skill_structure`, adds that each topic is stated in full in exactly one skill, its home.

**Test.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_is_home_of_routing_inspection_syntax_and_shared_gotchas]` covers each topic.

| Topic | What the test asserts |
| --- | --- |
| Routing | The `## Workflow` section contains the `| Task | Skill |` table. |
| Status and info | The `## Inspecting` section contains `` `habeas status [<selection>]` `` and `` `habeas info <selection>` ``. |
| Directive syntax | The `## Requirements, examples, and definitions` section describes the `{req}`, `{example}` and `{definition}` directives. |
| Reference syntax | The `## References` section has the "Write a reference with a full name…" text and the "Fence a reference" text. |
| Gotchas | The `## Gotchas` section contains the Git-index gotcha. |
| Distributed requirements | `references/distributed-requirements.md` exists and has the `# Distributed requirements` heading. |
| Syntax details | `references/syntax-details.md` exists and has the sections `## Full names in nested chapters` and `## Anchors`. |

The test then calls `assert_home("habeas")`, which does two things:

- It asserts that the whole bundled `habeas` skill (`SKILL.md` plus its references) contains every marker that `home_markers("habeas")` lists. The markers include the routing table, the selection syntax, fenced references, the `{violations}` and site-query text, the literal-text and `::::{req}` gotchas, and the coverage-artifacts text.
- It asserts that no other bundled skill contains any of those markers. This is the "exactly one home" check that `requirements.cli.skill_structure` requires.

**Why this is adequate.** Both halves of the obligation are checked: the `habeas` skill carries the topics, and no other skill restates them. The helpers `assert_text`, `section`, `skill_file`, `bundled_skill` and `home_markers` do real assertions, and each failure message names what is missing or restated. `section` is scoped to the heading and ignores headings inside code fences. The distributed-requirements topic is checked weakly in the named file, which has only a heading assertion. The `habeas` skill's own markers (site-query matches, `{violations}`) and the exclusivity check cover it further.

I read `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md`. It has the sections and text the test asserts, and the test would fail if they were removed or moved to another skill.

Nothing needs a {fixme}, and I found no obligation that goes untested.

text: Under {cite}`requirements.cli.skill_structure`, the `habeas` skill MUST be the home of routing tasks to skills, `habeas status` and `habeas info`, directive and reference syntax, distributed requirements, and gotchas common to every task.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST jointly give the direction that the requirements on them specify. A skill consists of its `SKILL.md` and the files under its `references/` directory. Each topic MUST be stated in full in exactly one skill, its home.
